title: Blaise Castle
text: A Gothic 'sham castle' built in 1766 by Robert Mylne for Thomas Farr: circular, with three turrets, on the site of a chapel of St Blaise whose last ruins were removed in 1707. The hill had earlier been an Iron Age hillfort, with Roman finds too.

title: Blaise Castle House
text: Built for the Quaker banker John Harford to designs by William Paty, after he bought the estate in 1789. John Nash added an orangery and C. R. Cockerell a picture room. Bristol City Council bought the estate in 1926; the house has been a museum since 1949.

title: The gorge and its caves
text: Humphry Repton laid out the park in the Hazel Brook gorge, with Lover's Leap, Goram's Chair, the Robber's Cave, Butcher's Cave, the Giant's Soapdish pool and the Penny Well.

title: Blaise Hamlet
text: Nine picturesque cottages round a green, designed by John Nash (with George Repton) for Harford's retired employees. The cottages and the sundial are all Grade I listed.
